title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 57 (Punishment for Personation of Shareholder)

content.overview: Section 57 provides that if any person deceitfully personates as an owner of any security or interest in a company, or of any share warrant or coupon issued in pursuance of this Act, and thereby obtains or attempts to obtain any such security or interest or any such share warrant or coupon, or receives or attempts to receive any money due to any such owner, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to three years and with fine which shall not be less than one lakh rupees but which may extend to five lakh rupees.
content.glance: Deceitful personation as owner of any security, interest, share warrant or coupon, to obtain (or attempt to obtain) the same or money due — imprisonment 1–3 years and fine ₹1–5 lakh.
content.study: If any person deceitfully personates as an owner of any security or interest in a company, or of any share warrant or coupon issued in pursuance of this Act, and thereby obtains or attempts to obtain any such security or interest or any such share warrant or coupon, or receives or attempts to receive any money due to any such owner, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to three years and with fine which shall not be less than one lakh rupees but which may extend to five lakh rupees. Current-law framing: prove deceitful personation as the owner; prove obtaining or attempting to obtain the security/interest/warrant/coupon, or receiving or attempting to receive money due to such owner; apply the statutory punishment range (imprisonment not less than one year and up to three years, and fine not less than one lakh and up to five lakh rupees).

sections.heading: Prohibited conduct
sections.body: Deceitfully personating as an owner of any security or interest in a company, or of any share warrant or coupon issued in pursuance of this Act.

sections.heading: Object of the personation
sections.body: Obtaining or attempting to obtain any such security or interest or any such share warrant or coupon, or receiving or attempting to receive any money due to any such owner.

sections.heading: Punishment
sections.body: Imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to three years, and fine which shall not be less than one lakh rupees but which may extend to five lakh rupees.

examples.title: Personation to obtain shares or dividend
examples.body: A person deceitfully pretends to be a registered shareholder and induces the company to issue a duplicate certificate or pay dividend. Section 57 is engaged.

examples.title: Attempt is punishable
examples.body: An attempt to obtain money due to a shareholder by deceitful personation as the owner is itself punishable under s. 57; success is not required.

hypotheticals.question: Is attempt enough under s. 57?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. The section covers obtaining or attempting to obtain the security, interest, warrant or coupon, and receiving or attempting to receive money due to the owner.

hypotheticals.question: Does the section apply only to shares?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. It covers any security or interest in a company, and any share warrant or coupon issued in pursuance of the Act.

misconceptions.trap: Only successful obtaining of shares is punishable.
misconceptions.correction: Section 57 also punishes attempts to obtain securities, warrants, coupons or money due by deceitful personation.

misconceptions.trap: The section is limited to share certificates.
misconceptions.correction: It covers any security or interest in a company, and any share warrant or coupon issued in pursuance of the Act.

Apply the statutory punishment range (imprisonment not less than one year and up to three years; fine not less than one lakh and up to five lakh rupees). IV. Distinguish from s. 38 where relevant. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions on a Section 57 charge contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Facts of deceitful personation as the owner; the security, interest, warrant or coupon involved; the obtain/attempt or receive/attempt of money due; identification of the true owner; the statutory punishment range; any connected offences.
